title: A Retrospective Observational Study of Health Facility Ownership Type and Performance on HIV Indicator Data Reporting in Kenya
d1_basis: Reporting completeness and timeliness are native DHIS2 reporting metrics at facility level, matching the data-generating unit.
d2_basis: Goal is association between facility ownership and reporting performance, directly represented by the extracted metrics.
d3_basis: Mann-Whitney comparisons address the stated ownership-group comparison; no unsupported longitudinal causal model is claimed.
d4_basis: Results are reported as performance differences without causal overreach.

title: All-Cause Mortality in Persons With HIV-HBV Co-Infection Treated for HBV in Rwanda: A Population-Based Cohort Study
d1_basis: Individual treatment records and hospital nesting are explicitly represented; multilevel modelling accounts for facility clustering.
d2_basis: Primary follow-up begins one year after HBV treatment initiation, yet the primary mortality target and title concern persons treated for HBV generally; first-year mortality is excluded from the main rate estimand.
d3_basis: Given the one-year-survivor cohort, multilevel Cox modelling is structurally appropriate and an all-treated sensitivity analysis is reported.
d4_basis: Conclusion calls the study population-based and generalizes the relatively low all-cause mortality rate to individuals treated for HBV in Rwanda although the main mortality-rate analysis conditions on surviving/remaining under observation for one year.

title: Analysis of pneumonia occurrence in relation to climate change in Tanga, Tanzania
d1_basis: Monthly HMIS pneumonia counts and monthly meteorological exposures are analysed at matching temporal and district levels.
d2_basis: The stated analytic goal is association between climate indicators and pneumonia occurrence.
d3_basis: Multilevel mixed-effects regression with an unstructured covariance structure addresses repeated temporal observations.
d4_basis: The paper states that the ecological study provided 'temporal causality' and moves from association to causal interpretation without a design that identifies causality.

title: Associations between natural resource extraction and incidence of acute and chronic health conditions in Tanzania
d1_basis: District-level DHIS2 outpatient counts are paired with census population denominators and health-facility counts; clustering over district-time is recognized.
d2_basis: Goal is explicitly framed as association between extraction projects and disease incidence.
d3_basis: Poisson models include period, population, region fixed effects, facility-time terms, cluster-robust standard errors and overdispersion handling.
d4_basis: Interpretation remains association-focused and limitations of routine HMIS data are acknowledged.

title: Combination of different intervention strategies for malaria mosquito vector control in Uganda: A review of secondary data of two districts with moderate to high disease transmission
d1_basis: Monthly tests, positives, intervention timing and meteorological covariates are observed consistently for the two comparison districts.
d2_basis: The target is intervention impact/effectiveness, but exposure contrasts arise from two non-randomized districts and changing intervention combinations rather than a design supporting the claimed causal estimand.
d3_basis: Difference-in-differences/ITS analyses rely on only two district clusters; one milestone uses standard OLS, no parallel-trends demonstration is reported, yet coefficients are treated as intervention effects.
d4_basis: The paper says covariate adjustment 'isolates the true operational effect' and concludes a compounding/protective benefit, exceeding what the observational two-district design supports.

title: Comparison of ARIMA and FB-Prophet time series models for the prediction of national and regional malaria incidence in Uganda
d1_basis: Population denominators and DHIS2 aggregation are described, but completeness and diagnostic/reporting changes are not sufficiently characterized to establish that routine counts support national/regional incidence without residual structural uncertainty.
d2_basis: Goal is forecasting malaria incidence and comparing forecast performance.
d3_basis: ARIMA and Prophet models use explicit training/validation periods and are compared using forecast-error metrics.
d4_basis: Forecast claims are bounded by acknowledged data-quality, aggregation, COVID-era and omitted-covariate limitations.

d2_basis: Target is data-quality assessment, directly matched to observed reporting and comparison data.
d3_basis: WHO-guided completeness/consistency checks and external comparisons are appropriate to the diagnostic target.
d4_basis: Conclusions accurately emphasize undercapture and data-quality limitations.

title: Hotspot Mapping, Spatiotemporal Clustering and Forecasting of Malaria Incidence in Uganda, 2014–2023
d1_basis: The paper recognizes that routine counts depend on reporting completeness, diagnostic practice and service use, but lacks auxiliary completeness/testing-volume data needed to establish those structures for the incidence series.
d2_basis: Goal is spatial heterogeneity, hotspot dynamics and probabilistic forecasting.
d3_basis: EHSA, trend analyses and ARIMA forecasting are explicitly separated into primary/exploratory components and forecasts are framed as continuation scenarios.
d4_basis: The paper explicitly avoids treating forecasts as real-time outbreak alerts and states that the 2018 spike cannot be uniquely interpreted.

title: Impact of accreditation on health care services performance in Kiryandongo district, Uganda: a longitudinal study
d1_basis: Quarterly indicators are observed within identified facilities and GEE accounts for within-facility clustering.
d2_basis: The target is causal impact of accreditation, but accreditation status is non-random and essentially contrasts one accredited facility with non-accredited facilities without an identification strategy for counterfactual accreditation effects.
d3_basis: GEE models repeated outcomes but does not address confounding by facility selection/accreditation or establish exchangeability; acknowledged unobserved facility differences remain.
d4_basis: The conclusion states that performance indicators were positively impacted by accreditation and that investment yields positive returns despite acknowledged unobserved-variable bias.

title: Impact of mass distribution of long-lasting insecticide nets on the incidence of malaria in Lomami, Democratic Republic of the Congo

d2_basis: Historical coding identified a causal impact target that the simple before/after observational comparison did not identify.
d3_basis: Historical coding identified simple pre/post t-tests as insufficient for the intervention-impact estimand.
d4_basis: Historical coding documented causal/impact interpretation despite non-significant incidence differences and inadequate causal design.

title: Impact of the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic on health services use in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
d1_basis: Facility reporting completeness is characterized; low-reporting facilities are excluded and the target is explicitly facility service use rather than population utilization.
d2_basis: Goal is interruption-associated change in essential health-service use, including the Gombe lockdown contrast.
d3_basis: Mixed-effects segmented Poisson interrupted-time-series models account for facility-level repeated observations and pre-pandemic trends.
d4_basis: Limitations explicitly prohibit population-level interpretation and acknowledge the short lockdown segment and incomplete facility coverage.

title: The use of routine health facility data for micro-stratification of malaria risk in mainland Tanzania
